sections.heading: Section 1: Location of Roots & Sign Change

questions.q: Show that the equation $x^3 - 2x - 5 = 0$ has a real root in the interval $[2, 3]$.
choices: $f(2) = -1 < 0$ and $f(3) = 16 > 0$, so by IVT a root exists
questions.answer: $f(2) = 8 - 4 - 5 = -1 < 0$. $f(3) = 27 - 6 - 5 = 16 > 0$. Since $f$ is continuous on $[2, 3]$ and changes sign, the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees at least one root.

questions.q: Under which condition does a sign change of $f(x)$ between $a$ and $b$ fail to guarantee a root in $(a, b)$?
choices: When $f(x)$ is not continuous on $[a, b]$
When the interval is wider than 1 unit
questions.answer: If $f(x)$ has a vertical asymptote or jump discontinuity in $(a, b)$ (e.g. $f(x) = 1/x$ between $-1$ and $1$), a sign change occurs without any root.

questions.q: Use the sign change method to determine which interval of length 0.1 contains the root of $x^3 = 20$.
Rearrange the equation $x^3 - x - 1 = 0$ into an iterative formula $x_{n+1} = g(x_n)$.
State the condition on $g'(x)$ for the iteration $x_{n+1} = g(x_n)$ to converge to a root $\alpha$.
questions.answer: Fixed-point iteration converges if and only if $|g'(x)| < 1$ in a neighborhood of the root $\alpha$.

questions.q: Starting with $x_1 = 1.3$, use $x_{n+1} = \sqrt[3]{x_n + 1}$ to calculate $x_2$ and $x_3$ correct to 3 decimal places.
If $0 < g'(\alpha) < 1$ at the root, what pattern is produced on the iteration diagram?
choices: A staircase diagram converging to the root
A cobweb diagram converging to the root
questions.answer: When the gradient $g'(x)$ is positive and less than 1, successive iterations approach the root monotonically from one side, forming a staircase diagram.

questions.q: If $-1 < g'(\alpha) < 0$ at the root, what pattern is produced on the iteration diagram?
questions.answer: A negative derivative between $-1$ and 0 causes the iterates to alternate sides around the root while decreasing in distance, forming an inward-spiraling cobweb.

choices: The iteration diverges away from the root
The iteration oscillates between two fixed values
questions.answer: If $|g'(\alpha)| > 1$, the fixed point is repulsive (unstable), and the sequence diverges away from $\alpha$.

questions.q: State the Newton-Raphson iteration formula for finding roots of $f(x) = 0$.
Use one iteration of Newton-Raphson with $x_0 = 2$ to approximate the root of $f(x) = x^2 - 5$.
Under which circumstance will the Newton-Raphson method fail completely at an iteration step $x_n$?
questions.answer: If $f'(x_n) = 0$, the tangent line is horizontal and never intersects the $x$-axis, causing division by zero in the formula.
